claims.text: At intermediate temperatures and moderate strain rates, Mn and Cr undergo stress-assisted, thermally activated diffusion in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Diffusing Mn and Cr form transient solute clusters or short-range-order regions during deformation.
Transient solute clusters temporarily pin or lock dislocations.
Dynamic solute pinning produces serrated flow through a dynamic strain-aging or Portevin-Le Chatelier-type mechanism.
Stronger solute pinning increases the stress required to remobilize dislocations.
The DSA regime raises the yield strength of Co-free FeNiCrMn relative to deformation governed only by forest hardening and lattice friction.
At elevated temperatures and lower strain rates, increased solute mobility dissolves the transient clusters.
Cluster dissolution promotes dynamic recovery, lowers strength, and increases ductility.
At lower temperatures or higher strain rates, diffusion is limited.
Limited diffusion at lower temperatures or higher strain rates leads to more effective dislocation pinning.
Co-free FeNiCrMn will exhibit a distinct serrated-flow regime at intermediate temperatures and moderate strain rates.
The proposed mechanism will produce a measurable shift in strain-rate sensitivity.
A fully homogenized Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy can be maintained as a single-phase FCC or equivalent solid solution without phase transformations throughout the test regime.
The relevant single-phase stability boundary is approximately -150 °C to 600 °C at strain rates from 10^-4 s^-1 to 10^-1 s^-1.
Serrations have been observed in other high-entropy alloys at about 10^-4 s^-1, at low temperatures, at 573–673 K, and in some cases at very high strain rates.
Several deformation mechanisms may overlap in high-entropy alloys, so serrated flow alone does not uniquely establish transient solute clustering.
A controlled temperature–strain-rate tensile-test matrix with microstructural measurements is proposed to compare the predicted DSA regime against behavior without dynamic clustering.
Failure to observe transient clusters in the predicted regime, or serrated flow indistinguishable from a clustering-absent control, is defined as falsifying the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The central account says thermally activated diffusion is needed to form clusters and pin dislocations at intermediate temperatures, but the mechanism field also says that lower temperatures or higher strain rates, where diffusion is limited, produce more effective pinning. No alternative non-diffusive source of the stronger pinning is supplied.

Pinning and strengthening are assigned primarily to an intermediate-temperature/moderate-rate regime, yet the mechanism field extends more effective pinning toward lower temperatures and higher rates without specifying whether strength and serration amplitude should peak there or in the stated intermediate regime.
